function.mechanism: Provides free glutamate that enhances umami (savory) taste.

adi.basis: Group ADI for glutamic acid and glutamates (E620-E625), expressed as glutamic acid, derived from NOAEL 3200 mg MSG/kg bw/day with UF 100 (EFSA 2017).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded exposure can exceed the ADI in some population groups and recommended reviewing maximum permitted levels.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group ADI context for L-glutamic acid and its salts in WHO JECFA entry).

concerns.summary: A 2025 rat overconsumption study (0.8-3 g/kg bw/day for 8 weeks) reported dose-dependent hepatic, renal, and cardiac toxicity markers and histopathology.
A 2024 systematic review reported possible links between MSG exposure and gut microbiota/metabolic dysbiosis, but evidence was limited and largely preclinical.
In controlled human challenge data, large bolus doses without food may trigger transient symptoms in some self-identified sensitive individuals, with inconsistent reproducibility.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA found no concern for genotoxicity for glutamic acid and glutamates (E620-E625).
A 2025 publication of GLP-style 28-day and 90-day dietary rat studies reported no toxicologically significant findings up to the highest tested doses (NOAEL at top dose).

populations: high consumers across population groups (EFSA refined assessment)
toddlers and children at medium exposure
highly exposed infants, children, and adolescents
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported potential exceedance of the 30 mg/kg bw/day group ADI in several scenarios; a 2023 China assessment estimated 17.63 mg/kg bw/day from measured data and 40.20 mg/kg bw/day from apparent-consumption data.

risk_assessment.rationale: MSG remains widely authorized (EU authorized with EFSA re-evaluation, FDA GRAS, JECFA ADI not specified), but EFSA established a finite ADI and identified exceedance risk in some populations, and high-dose literature still reports adverse findings.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day with exceedance concern
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR with GMP and labeling requirements
No IARC Monographs group classification identified
Mixed newer safety literature including high-dose animal toxicity reports
